critical_path: Hard dependencies: Telemetry audit must finish before study annotation begins (hard); design drafts cannot proceed without evidence traceability (hard). Soft dependencies: Survey bias analysis can run in parallel with telemetry audit but must be completed before recommendation framing (soft). The critical path is: Telemetry Audit → Study Annotation → Recommendation Framing → Prototype Build → Final Flow Approval. Duration: 12 weeks total, derived from sequential hard dependencies; slip threshold at 3 days beyond the end of Phase 2 triggers recomputation of the entire critical path. Any delay in telemetry audit or study annotation will directly impact all downstream workstreams.
decision_log: Decision: To pair telemetry with moderated study findings for onboarding redesign. Evidence basis: Telemetry shows 68% drop-off at Step 3; moderated sessions confirm users skip tutorial due to perceived complexity. Risk if assumption wrong: Users may still skip tutorial despite changes, leading to poor first-value adoption. Decision: To discount double-count defect in telemetry data at Step 4. Evidence basis: Instrumentation log confirms double-count on Step 4 for two quarters. Risk if assumption wrong: Funnel drop-off appears lower than actual; redesign may fail to address real user behavior. Decision: To use persona-level segment definitions from survey before deriving any percentage. Evidence basis: Survey shows skew in responses by persona (e.g., 340 responses, 12% from non-technical users). Risk if assumption wrong: Percentages derived from skewed segments will misrepresent true drop-off rates. Decision: To require every recommendation to name its evidence line and the risk of incorrect assumption. Evidence basis: Reviewer feedback on prior designs citing no evidence. Risk if assumption wrong: Design decisions lack traceability, leading to poor user outcomes or regulatory issues.
